content: 1. A reduced dose of cobimetinib (40 mg or 20 mg daily) is recommended when necessary. 2. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of colchicine by mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Coadministration of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 3. Conivaptan increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while cortisone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Crizotinib and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Cyclosporine increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the level or effect of cyclosporine by the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Erythromycin base increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Darifenacin increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the level or effect of darifenacin by the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Darunavir increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Dasatinib increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the level or effect of dasatinib by the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Degarelix and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Desflurane and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Desipramine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. DHEA (herbal) increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Diltiazem increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the level or effect of diltiazem by the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If no alternative is available, monitor for diltiazem effects following erythromycin initiation or discontinuation. 20. Dofetilide and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Donepezil and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Doxepin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Dronedarone increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the level or effect of dronedarone by the same mechanism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Droperidol and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 26. Efavirenz decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 29. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat poor or intermediate metabolizers; reduce eliglustat dose from 84 mg BID to 84 mg once daily in extensive metabolizers. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 30. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Decrease eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 31. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use of a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce encorafenib dose to one-half of the dose (e.g., reduce from 450 mg/day to 225 mg/day). Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 32. Erythromycin base increases the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Erythromycin base and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 34. Enzalutamide decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Epinephrine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Racemic epinephrine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Erdafitinib increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after administration of P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 38. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Eribulin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 40. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 49. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 52. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fentanyl (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 53. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fentanyl (transdermal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 54. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fentanyl (transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 55. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and coadministration may increase the risk for adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 57. Fingolimod and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while fludrocortisone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Fluphenazine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 60. Erythromycin base increases the effects of fondaparinux by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Erythromycin base and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and fosamprenavir increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Fosaprepitant increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base increases the level or effect of fosaprepitant by the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 64. Fosphenytoin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 65. Gemifloxacin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 66. Gilteritinib and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 67. Erythromycin base and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unable to avoid coadministration, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 68. Erythromycin base and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 69. Granisetron and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 70. Grapefruit increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 71. Griseofulvin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 72. Erythromycin base and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 73. Erythromycin base increases the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 74. Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 75. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
